agents.name: KYOU
agents.short_description: Finds Japanese stocks moving now through price acceleration, volume expansion, and short-term breakout pressure.
weaknesses: Can enter after a move has already extended
Needs strict exits to avoid stale momentum trades

agents.name: NAGARE
agents.short_description: Follows medium-term trend structure and tries to hold winners while the broader flow remains intact.
weaknesses: Slower to exit reversals
May underperform in choppy tape

agents.name: MAMORU
agents.short_description: Prioritizes liquidity, drawdown control, volatility discipline, and capital preservation.
weaknesses: Can miss high-beta winners
May sell too early when volatility rises

agents.name: SAGURI
agents.short_description: Searches smaller and less-discovered names for early volume shifts and hidden alpha signals.
strengths: Finds names before they become obvious
weaknesses: Liquidity risk is structurally higher
Requires fast exits when small-cap interest disappears

agents.name: MATSU
agents.short_description: Waits for controlled pullbacks inside still-healthy trends rather than chasing heat.
strengths: Looks for better risk/reward entry points
weaknesses: May wait too long
Can confuse pullbacks with trend breaks without strict risk rules

agents.name: KAESHI
agents.short_description: Hunts short, sharp rebounds after oversold pressure and exhaustion-style setups.
weaknesses: Reversal trades can fail quickly
Should not overstay after the bounce normalizes

agents.name: HIZUMI
agents.short_description: Looks for price/value distortion, conservative re-rating setups, and trap-aware value signals.
strengths: Differentiates price action from value distortion
weaknesses: Full strength requires better fundamentals data
Must avoid value traps
